<a id="CancellationKey"></a>

### Key of a cancellation's refund

`CancellationKey` · `src/architecture.ts:143`

The idempotency key the provider receives: this prefix, then the reservation. A request repeated for the same reservation refunds only once.

- Value: cancellation-

- Decided by: karim
- Used by: [Cancel a reservation](api.md#CancelReservation)
- Applies: [A cancellation refunds once](principles.md#RefundOnce)

## Architecture rules

<a id="ReadWithoutWrite"></a>

### A read writes nothing

`ReadWithoutWrite` · `src/architecture.ts:161` · status: **held**

A GET writes neither to the database nor to a third party, not even through a distant dependency.

Respected everywhere.

<details><summary>The rule, in code</summary>

```ts
(g: Graph) =>
    g.all("entry").nodes()
      .filter((v) => isRead(v.field("trigger") as Trigger))
      .flatMap((v) => v.effects.filter((e) => e === "write" || e === "third-party").map((e) => ({ on: v, what: `A read has the effect "${e}"` })))
```

</details>

- Owner: karim

<a id="ThirdPartiesVerified"></a>

### Every call to a third party is verified

`ThirdPartiesVerified` · `src/architecture.ts:186` · status: **held**

An entry point that calls a third party has at least one scenario that verifies it.

Respected everywhere.

<details><summary>The rule, in code</summary>

```ts
(g: Graph) =>
    g.all("entry").nodes()
      .filter((v) => v.effects.includes("third-party") && !g.from(v).in("verifies").exists())
      .map((v) => ({ on: v, what: "Calls a third party without a scenario that verifies it" }))
```

</details>

- Owner: karim

<a id="UtilitiesWithoutWorld"></a>

### Utilities do not touch the world

`UtilitiesWithoutWorld` · `src/architecture.ts:175` · status: **held**

A utility function neither reads nor writes the database, and does not call the network. Reading the time is allowed. A function that answers a port (a repository over the database port) is not a utility: it is a realization, chosen by a technical choice.

Respected everywhere.

<details><summary>The rule, in code</summary>

```ts
(g: Graph) =>
    g.all("function").where((v) => !g.from(v).out("implements").exists()).nodes().flatMap((v) =>
      v.effects.filter((e) => ["read", "write", "network", "third-party"].includes(e)).map((e) => ({ on: v, what: `A utility has the effect "${e}"` })))
```

</details>

- Owner: karim
